heard: Exposed to the vacuum of space, your body does not explode. Popular movies love to show astronauts bursting like fragile balloons when their pressurized suits fail completely. In December 1966, NASA test subject Jim LeBlanc tested this terrifying theory. His spacesuit hose accidentally detached inside a massive altitude vacuum chamber. LeBlanc remained conscious for about 14 seconds before severe hypoxia completely set in. His very last conscious memory was feeling the warm saliva on his tongue start to bubble. A quick colleague entered the chamber within 25 seconds to provide emergency oxygen. Human skin is remarkably elastic enough to prove that your body does not explode.
